destinations.name: Cape Coast Castle
destinations.summary: Historic coastal fortress and UNESCO World Heritage site documenting transatlantic trade history.
destinations.description: Cape Coast Castle is one of approximately forty 'slave castles' built on the Gold Coast of West Africa. Originally built by Swedish traders for timber and gold trade, it was later used extensively in the trans-Atlantic slave trade.
destinations.culturalHistory: Under British colonial administration, the castle became the central headquarters of British Gold Coast possessions until the capital moved to Christianborg Castle in Accra in 1877.

media.altText: View of the ramparts and historic cannons overlooking the Gulf of Guinea at Cape Coast Castle
media.caption: Historic ramparts overlooking the Atlantic coastline

destinations.name: Elmina Castle
destinations.summary: The oldest European building in existence south of the Sahara, erected by the Portuguese in 1482.
destinations.description: São Jorge da Mina (Elmina Castle) was established as a trade settlement before becoming a major pivot point on the Atlantic slave route.
destinations.culturalHistory: Captured by the Dutch West India Company in 1637 and ceded to Britain in 1872. Recognized by UNESCO as a monument of global memory.

media.altText: Exterior whitewashed walls and stone towers of Elmina Castle on the Atlantic bay
media.caption: Courtyard and sea bastions of Elmina Castle

destinations.name: Manhyia Palace Museum
destinations.summary: The official seat of the Asantehene, chronicling the rich legacy and regalia of the Ashanti Kingdom.
destinations.description: Built by the British in 1925 for Asantehene Prempeh I upon his return from exile in the Seychelles. The museum houses authentic royal artifacts, drums, palanquins, and historic peace treaty documents.
destinations.culturalHistory: Serves as the focal center of the vibrant Asante culture, showcasing dynastic lineages, golden stools, and diplomatic history.

media.altText: Entrance courtyard and historic architecture of the Manhyia Palace grounds
media.caption: Prempeh I historical building inside Manhyia grounds

destinations.name: Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park
destinations.summary: National monument and mausoleum dedicated to Ghana's first President and Pan-African visionary.
destinations.description: Located in downtown Accra on the former British colonial polo grounds where Kwame Nkrumah declared Ghana's independence in 1957. Recently renovated with state-of-the-art interactive exhibits and fountains.
destinations.culturalHistory: The mausoleum is designed to resemble an upside-down sword, symbolizing peace in Akan traditional symbolism.

media.altText: Statue and marble fountains at the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park in Accra
media.caption: Presidential mausoleum and water gardens

destinations.name: W.E.B. Du Bois Memorial Centre
destinations.summary: Former home and resting place of the pioneering African American sociologist and Pan-Africanist.
destinations.description: The sanctuary preserves the personal library, academic manuscripts, and memorabilia of Dr. William Edward Burghardt Du Bois, who relocated to Ghana at the invitation of Kwame Nkrumah to edit the Encyclopedia Africana.
destinations.culturalHistory: Du Bois spent his final years here and was laid to rest beside his wife Shirley Graham Du Bois on the grounds.

media.altText: Garden pathways and memorial building at the W.E.B. Du Bois Memorial Centre
media.caption: Du Bois research library and memorial complex

destinations.name: Jamestown, Ussher Fort and Lighthouse
destinations.summary: Vibrant coastal Ga fishing community steeped in British-Ga maritime history and boxing heritage.
destinations.description: Jamestown is one of Accra's oldest districts, famous for its red-and-white colonial lighthouse, traditional harbor fishing canoes, and colonial-era trading forts.
destinations.culturalHistory: Home to the Chale Wote Street Art Festival and widely celebrated worldwide for generating numerous world boxing champions.
destinations.address: High Street & Cleland Road, Jamestown, Accra, Ghana

media.altText: The iconic red and white Jamestown lighthouse in Accra against the Atlantic ocean
media.caption: Jamestown colonial lighthouse overlooking fishing harbor

destinations.name: Independence Arch & Black Star Square
destinations.summary: Massive public ceremonial ground framed by the iconic Independence Arch and eternal flame of African liberation.
destinations.description: Commissioned by Kwame Nkrumah to celebrate national sovereignty. It remains the venue for national Independence Day celebrations every March 6th and major civic assemblies.
destinations.culturalHistory: The Black Star atop the arch was adopted as a symbol of African freedom, unity, and resilience.

media.altText: The grand Independence Arch with the Black Star symbol standing in Accra
media.caption: The Independence Arch in Accra

destinations.name: Fort St. Jago
destinations.summary: Hilltop fortress overlooking Elmina Castle and the Atlantic port, built for strategic artillery defense.
destinations.description: Built by the Dutch in the 1660s on St. Jago Hill opposite Elmina Castle to prevent rival forces from bombarding the castle from above.
destinations.culturalHistory: Offers one of the most stunning panoramic views of the Gulf of Guinea and the historic town of Elmina.

media.altText: Stone ramparts of Fort St. Jago on the hill looking towards Elmina harbor
media.caption: Hilltop artillery fort overlooking Elmina

destinations.name: Larabanga Mosque
destinations.summary: Ancient Sudanese architectural wonder founded in 1421, regarded as the 'Mecca of West Africa'.
destinations.description: Constructed with packed mud and timber logs in the traditional Sudano-Sahelian style. Houses a sacred 17th-century Quran and is the oldest mosque in Ghana.
destinations.culturalHistory: Surrounded by legends of an invisible hand that aided its founding mystic, Ayuba, in its construction.
destinations.address: Larabanga, near Damongo, Savannah Region, Ghana

media.altText: Traditional whitewashed mud and timber architecture of Larabanga Mosque
media.caption: Larabanga Mosque's distinctive buttresses and timber spires

destinations.name: Nzulezu Stilt Village
destinations.summary: An extraordinary 400-year-old settlement constructed entirely on stilts over Lake Tadane.
destinations.description: Nzulezu, meaning 'surface of water' in the Nzema language, was built by ancestors migrating from the ancient Walata Empire following a divine snail guide.
destinations.culturalHistory: Daily community life, schools, churches, and meeting places exist perched on wooden stilts interconnected by footbridges.
destinations.address: Beyin Canal Departure, Western Region, Ghana

media.altText: Wooden walkways and thatched homes built on stilts over tranquil lake waters in Nzulezu
media.caption: Stilt structures over Lake Tadane

destinations.name: Aqua Safari Resort
destinations.summary: Luxury waterfront resort situated along the Volta River estuary in Ada Foah.
destinations.description: A premier coastal luxury getaway featuring tranquil boat cruises, water skiing, marine wildlife encounters, and serene river chalets.

media.altText: Riverfront swimming pool and chalets along the serene Volta riverbank
media.caption: Waterfront accommodations at Aqua Safari

destinations.description: An extraordinary nature resort blending five-star hospitality with equestrian trails, exotic wildlife, organic farm-to-table dining, and wellness retreats.

media.altText: Verdant green valleys and luxury stone bungalows at Safari Valley Resort
media.caption: Scenic landscapes in the Okere hills

media.altText: Island swimming pool surrounded by palm trees and tranquil river waters
media.caption: Island leisure and water activities

destinations.description: Tented luxury suites with infinity swimming pools where elephants gather below to drink. Offers guided walking safaris and game drives.

media.caption: Overlooking the animal watering hole in Mole

media.altText: Tropical gardens and lagoon swimming pools at Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra
media.caption: Poolside and beachfront grounds at Labadi

destinations.name: La Palm Royal Beach Hotel

media.caption: Sunset over the Atlantic at La Palm

destinations.name: Coconut Grove Beach Resort
destinations.summary: Picturesque coastal resort in Elmina with private ocean frontage and coconut palm groves.
destinations.description: Located near Elmina Castle and Kakum National Park, offering horse riding on the beach, an ocean golf course, fresh seafood, and peaceful sea breezes.
destinations.address: Bridge House, Elmina, Central Region, Ghana

media.altText: Palm trees and golden sand beach at Coconut Grove Resort in Elmina
media.caption: Golden sands and private shoreline in Elmina

destinations.name: Mole National Park
destinations.summary: Ghana's largest and most famous wildlife refuge, home to African elephants, antelopes, and baboons.
destinations.description: Encompassing over 4,500 square kilometres of Guinea savannah woodland, Mole offers unique foot safaris guided by armed wildlife rangers, allowing close-up encounters with peaceful elephant herds.
destinations.culturalHistory: Established in 1958 as a game reserve and upgraded to a national park in 1971. Features the historic Konkori escarpment and watering holes.
destinations.address: Mole National Park, Savannah Region, Ghana

media.altText: Elephants walking through savannah grassland in Mole National Park
media.caption: Elephants near the watering hole in Mole

destinations.name: Kakum National Park
destinations.summary: Dense coastal rainforest celebrated for its exhilarating canopy walkway suspended 40 metres above the forest floor.
destinations.description: The 350-metre-long canopy walkway offers a bird's-eye view of virgin rainforest canopy teeming with butterflies, monkeys, hornbills, and medicinal forest trees.
destinations.culturalHistory: Managed with local Assin communities, preserving indigenous herbal medicine knowledge and ancestral rainforest conservation.
destinations.address: Cape Coast - Twifo Praso Road, Central Region, Ghana

media.altText: Hanging canopy walkway bridge suspended between giant hardwood trees in Kakum rainforest
media.caption: Canopy walkway 40 metres above the forest floor

destinations.name: Shai Hills Resource Reserve
destinations.summary: Rugged granite rocky hills, ancestral caves, baboon troops, and zebras located just an hour outside Accra.
destinations.description: An accessible eco-excursion offering rock climbing, cycling, hiking, and visits to the ancestral caves where the Shai people lived before 1892.
destinations.culturalHistory: The caves served as a natural fortress during regional wars and retain ancestral archaeological remains.
destinations.address: Tema-Akosombo Road, Doryumu, Greater Accra, Ghana

media.altText: Granite inselbergs and savannah scrub at Shai Hills Resource Reserve
media.caption: Granite inselbergs across Shai Hills plains
